(p-245) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Qalam (The Pen)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nun﴾.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already discussed the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah, the letters that open certain surahs) at the beginning of the commentary on the first surah of Hud. He mentioned all the opinions on them, and they are five:

It has been said that they are among the things whose knowledge Allah has kept to Himself; or that they are among the names of Allah; or that they are composed of several letters, each letter standing for a word; or that they are names of the surahs; or that they are for i'jaz (the inimitability of the Qur'an). He explained the reasoning behind each of these views, and he preferred the last, that they are for i'jaz, on the evidence that what follows them is always a defence of the Qur'an. He expounded the discussion sufficiently and satisfactorily.

Ibn Kathir mentioned other opinions, among them that nun means the inkwell (al-dawah), i.e., because of the mention of the pen. He attributed this to al-Hasan and Qatadah, and said that there is a marfu' hadith on it, but it is very gharib (weak/odd). It is from Ibn 'Abbas: "Allah created the nun, which is the inkwell, and He created the pen, and said to it: Write," and the hadith continues.

And from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah created the nun, which is the inkwell."

Ibn Jarir mentioned all these aspects and added other aspects: among them, that they are openings of the beginnings of surahs that draw the attention of the listeners, after which what follows them is recited to them. It was also said that they are from the reckoning of the abjad (al-jumal, the numerical value of letters), and other things.

Ibn Jarir, at the beginning of "Surat al-Shura," mentioned: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿'Ayn Sin Qaf﴾ [al-Shura: 1-2], a report that Ibn Kathir quoted from him and found strange and disapproved of, but there has occurred something close to its fulfilment and a complete correspondence with it.

Its text from Ibn Jarir: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said to him, while Huzayfah ibn al-Yaman was with him: Tell me about the interpretation of Allah's saying: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿'Ayn Sin Qaf﴾. He lowered his head, then turned away from him. Then he repeated his question, and he turned away and did not answer him with anything, and disliked his question. Then he repeated it a third time, and he did not answer him at all.

(p-246) Huzayfah said to him: I will tell you about them, for I know why he disliked it. It was revealed concerning a man from his household called Abd al-Ilah or Abd Allah, who will descend upon a river of the rivers of the East, on which two cities are built. He will split the river between them with a split. When Allah permits the end of their rule and the cutting off of their dynasty and their cities, Allah will send a fire upon one of the two cities at night, and in the morning it will be black and dark, burnt, as if it had never been in its place. Its companion will wake up amazed how it escaped. Nothing will happen but the brightness of that day until every stubborn tyrant among them is gathered in it. Then Allah will cause it to sink with them all. This is His saying: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿'Ayn Sin Qaf﴾, meaning a decree from Allah, a trial, and a judgement.

﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿'Ayn Sin Qaf﴾, meaning His justice: Sin means "sayakun" (it will be), and Qaf means "waqi'" (it will befall) upon these two cities. End quote.

Although Ibn Kathir found this strange and disapproved of it, something similar to what the hadith indicates has occurred in the uprising in Iraq against Abd al-Ilah in Baghdad, where the river splits it into two parts, and he is from the Family of the House, and what was described in the mentioned report has indeed happened there.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 2 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾ ﴿And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off﴾ ﴿And indeed, you are of a tremendous character﴾.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and on him, had already explained the refutation of their claim when commenting on His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "There is in him madness"? Rather, he has brought them the truth﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:70], in the surah of "al-Mu'minun."

He cited the texts and said: "In the verse there is what refutes them, which is His saying, ﴿Rather, he has brought them the truth.﴾" End of quote.

Likewise here, in this verse, there is what indicates the falsehood of their claim and refutes them, which is His saying, ﴿And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off﴾, meaning: for what you brought of the truth, and for your carrying out of the conveyance of the message from Allah and your patience in it. This is as He refuted them with His saying, ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾ [al-Takwir 81:22].

Similarly, His saying concerning His noble and greatest Messenger: ﴿And indeed, you are of a tremendous character﴾, because the madman is a fool who does not mean what he says and does not handle any affair well.

The "tremendous character" (al-khuluq al-'azim) is the highest rank of perfection among great men.

As for His saying, ﴿And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off﴾: al-mann (المَنّ) means cutting off. That is, his reward (ﷺ) with Allah is not interrupted.

The poet said:

*For a mauled, hunting dog, whose prey's flesh is torn between it and fierce, predatory wolves, whose food is never cut off (or given grudgingly).*

Allah the Exalted has explained the continuity of his reward without interruption in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:56].

The blessings of Allah upon him, and the blessings of the angels and the believers, do not cease by night or by day. They are, from Allah, mercy, and from the angels and the believers, supplication.

In the two surahs "al-Duha" and "Alam Nashrah" in their entirety: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾ ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha 93:3-5].

And His saying: ﴿And We raised high for you your remembrance﴾ [al-Sharh 94:4].

It is known from the Sunnah that whoever guides to good has a reward like that of whoever acts upon it. There is no Muslim for whom a good deed is recorded in his record except that the Messenger (ﷺ) has a like reward for it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except from three," and among them: "or knowledge from which benefit is derived." And what knowledge is more widely beneficial than what he (ﷺ) brought and left among the Ummah? Until he said: "I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah and my Sunnah." And beyond that are the texts that indicate the continuity of his reward.

As for his recompense with Allah, none knows its measure except Allah the Exalted.

As for His saying, ﴿And indeed, you are of a tremendous character﴾: it has been mentioned that this is in the position of a refutation of the initial claim of the polytheists against him (ﷺ) and their accusation of him with madness, because the characters of madmen are blameworthy, rather they have no character at all. Here is the highest level of elevation in character.

This context has also been emphasized by several affirmative devices: its inclusion within the answer to the first oath at the beginning of the surah; the lam in (لَعَلى, "la-'ala"); and the use of 'ala (عَلى), which indicates elevation and firm establishment, instead of "dhu" (ذُو, "possessor of"), as in the phrase "dhu khuluqin 'azim" (possessor of a tremendous character). This is to show the strength of firm establishment and elevation, and that he (ﷺ) is above every tremendous character, firmly established in it and elevated over it.

The tremendous character has been mentioned here in summary, and it is among the most general of the qualities with which Allah praised His Messenger (ﷺ) in His Book. 'Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) pointed to what explained this summary when she was asked about his (ﷺ) character, for which he was praised, and she said: "His character was the Qur'an," meaning, and Allah knows best: he (ﷺ) would carry out its commands and refrain from its prohibitions, as in His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from﴾ [al-Hashr 59:7].

And as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ [al-Isra' 17:9].

And as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "None of you believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought."

So he (ﷺ) was, in his whole conduct, complying with the teachings of the Qur'an, and he has been commanded to take him as a model, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. Therefore, among the most important things required of the Ummah is knowing the details of this summary, so that the required emulation may be completed.

The matter of character in general, and his (ﷺ) character in particular, has taken the foremost place in the investigations of researchers and the instructions of guides. For the public, it is the foundation of the stability of nations and the factor in preserving their survival, as it was said:

*Nations are only their character, so long as it remains; if their character departs, they depart.*

The Prophet (ﷺ) summarized his entire mission in noble character in his saying (ﷺ): "I was only sent to perfect noble character."

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), may Allah's pleasure be upon them, took care of the matter of his character after the revelation of this verse, and they asked 'Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) about that, and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." Scholars have also devoted works to it, such as the "Shama'il" of al-Tirmidhi.

As for the statements of the exegetes concerning the tremendous character meant here, they are of two views, with no contradiction between them:

Among them: that it is the religion (al-din). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi, and others.

The other is the statement of 'Aishah: "His character was the Qur'an." The Qur'an and the religion are linked. However, the summary remained present. When we return to some verses of the Qur'an, we find some explanation of what he (ﷺ) possessed of great character, such as His saying:

﴿Take what is easy, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf 7:199].

And His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer; he is solicitous over you; for the believers, he is kind and merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:128].

And His saying: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient with them. And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have disbanded from around you. So pardon them﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:159].

And His saying: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a manner that is best﴾ [al-Nahl 16:125].

And like these are the verses containing guidance or description with what is the greatest of characters. And if his (ﷺ) character was the Qur'an, then the Qur'an guides to that which is most upright.

The one who reflects on the Qur'an in its guidance finds the principle of character in every legislation within it, even in acts of worship. In prayer there is humility, submission, tranquility, and dignity; so come to it with tranquility and dignity upon you. In zakat there is manliness and generosity. ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:264].

And His saying: ﴿We only feed you for the countenance of Allah. We do not want from you reward or gratitude﴾ [al-Insan 76:9].

And in fasting: "Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need that he should give up his food and drink."

And His saying (ﷺ): "Fasting is a shield."

And in Hajj: ﴿So there shall be no sexual immorality, defiance, or quarreling during Hajj﴾.

And in social matters: the Prophet (ﷺ) was addressed with the highest degrees of character, even if he was not directly within the address, since he is not outside the scope of the demand: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾, then after it comes ﴿Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them [so much as], "uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word﴾ ﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:23-24], although neither of his parents was alive at the time of its revelation. And beyond that are the general and specific teachings that the Qur'an includes.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was concerned with character to the point that he would instruct it to those he sent out everywhere, as he instructed Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) with his saying: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow the bad deed with a good deed to erase it, and deal with people with good character."

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Among what people have gotten from the words of prophethood: if you have no shame, then do what you wish." That is, shame, which is among the most distinctive of characters, is a fence against vices. This confirms that good character leads to virtues and prevents vices, as it was said:

*Indeed, the noble man, when he is able to harm, the character of the noble comes to him and he refrains.*

*And you see the base man, when he is able to harm, he transgresses and leaves no place for reconciliation.*

The Qur'an has pointed to this aspect in His saying: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon people; and Allah loves the doers of good﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:134].

Note

Among the most important matters of character is his (ﷺ) explanation of it in his saying: "I was only sent to perfect noble character."

Yet his mission was with monotheism, acts of worship, transactions, and other things that make character a part of the mission.

The explanation of this is in a categorical, logical, predicative syllogism (qadiyya mantiqiyya qat'iyya hamliyya). Its major premise (muqaddima, here the minor premise, al-sughra) is a sound hadith: "Religion is good character." The major premise (al-kubra) is the noble verse: His saying, ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets, and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing slaves; and [who] establishes prayer and gives zakah; and those who fulfill their promise when they promise; and the patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:177].

Because the two terms of the minor premise are equal in extension (al-masdaq, the set of things to which a term applies), namely "Religion is good character," the logical structure by the conjunctive syllogism (al-qiyas al-iqtirani, the syllogism formed by joining premises) becomes: good character is righteousness, and righteousness is belief in Allah and the Last Day, and what is connected to it, to the end of what came in the noble verse. The conclusion is: good character is belief in Allah and the Last Day and what is connected to it.

This noble verse included the whole religion in its three divisions:

Islam, including prayer and zakat, etc.

Faith in Allah, His angels, etc.

And good conduct in fulfilling promises, truthfulness, patience, and God-consciousness (taqwa), which is watchfulness of Allah in secret and in public. The result of the greatness of these characters has appeared in the general, comprehensive mercy in His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:107].

Likewise, [it is a mercy] for the Ummah on the Day of Resurrection, as he (ﷺ) said: "The nearest of you to me in rank on the Day of Resurrection are the best of you in character."

This is another logical matter: "I was only sent to perfect noble character," and ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾.

So the noble characters are a mercy to the worlds in this life, and an exalted station for the believers in the Hereafter.

* *

Another note.

The scholars of sociology agree that the foundations of character are four:

They are: wisdom, chastity, courage, and justice.

Opposed to them are four vices:

They are: ignorance, greed, cowardice, and injustice.

From each virtue branch its sub-branches:

From wisdom: intelligence, ease of understanding, and breadth of knowledge. From chastity: contentment, scrupulousness, modesty, generosity, tranquility, patience, and freedom. From courage: boldness and greatness of aspiration. From magnanimity: generosity, selflessness, consolation, and forgiveness.

As for justice, which is the mother of the moral virtues, there branch from it: friendship, affection, maintaining family ties, abandoning spite, repaying evil with good, and using gentleness. These are the roots of character and its branches, and no trait of them remains except that it is complete in him (ﷺ).

Allah has cleared him of every vice, so it is established that he (ﷺ) was of a tremendous character, in deed and in intellect.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: "He (ﷺ) was indeed of a tremendous character. Character is that with which a person has been molded (takhallaqa), because Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am 6:90], and every prophet must have a virtuous trait. Thus all the qualities of virtue were gathered for him (ﷺ) that were in all the prophets." This has a basis, but the actual reality of his (ﷺ) biography is more comprehensive than that.

Before the mission and the revelation, he was called "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy) by the Quraysh, as in the story of placing the Black Stone in the Ka'bah, when they said of him: "Al-Amin; we are pleased with him."

And there is related from Zayd ibn Harithah, when he was taken captive and Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, gifted him to serve the Prophet ﷺ. His family came with the ransom, seeking to redeem him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said to them: "Call him and inform him. If he chooses you, then he is yours without ransom." Zayd said: "By Allah, I will never choose anyone over your companionship, ever." His family said to him: "Woe to you! Would you choose slavery over freedom?!" He said: "Yes, by Allah, I have been in his company, and he has never said to me regarding anything I did: 'Why did you do it?', nor regarding anything I did not do: 'Why did you not do it?'" His people returned, and he remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he took him by the hand and announced his adoption of him, in accordance with what was customary before the Prophethood.

Indeed, if we were to say: Allah's choosing of him was before his existence, and Allah's care for him after his existence, from the splitting of his chest in his childhood, and from the death of his parents and Allah's guardianship of him, that would be correct.

As in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And He found you lost and guided you? And He found you poor and made you self-sufficient? So as for the orphan, do not oppress him; and as for the beggar, do not repel him; and as for the favor of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [Ad-Duha: 3–11].

It is a blessing of Allah Exalted upon him and upon his Ummah along with him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and may He grant us the ability to follow his example.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾ ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ ﴿And do not obey every oft-swearing contemptible one﴾ ﴿A slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾ ﴿Forbidder of good, transgressor, sinful﴾ ﴿Brutal, and after that, of illegitimate birth﴾ ﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾ ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients"﴾ ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾ (p-253)

If the verse before this one, ﴿And indeed you are of a magnificent character﴾, came before it, then it is a rebuttal of their false claim against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he was possessed.

In this verse there is the declaring of his (ﷺ) innocence from the vile qualities and defects they possess, and the exposure of them, and the explanation of the difference and the vast gulf between him and them. At the same time that He described him as being of a magnificent character, He described them with the opposite of that: lying, compromising, excessive swearing, contemptibility, defamation, going about with malicious talk, forbidding good, brutality, arrogance, transgression, wrongdoing, and illegitimacy, ten blameworthy traits. Their result is branding with disgrace upon the noses, as humiliation for them.

The verses of the Qur'an have come explaining the evils of those traits and warning against them. It is not possible for us to cite all of them, and an indication to some of them suffices, as a reminder of all of them, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; and let not women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not defame one another or call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11-12].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾

Al-Qurtubi mentioned for the meanings of al-mudahana (compromise) more than ten sayings, the most preferred of which is al-mulayana (softness/leniency). Here He mentioned their wishing and desire for compromise, and He did not mention for us whether he (ﷺ) compromised with them or not, nor whether they intended by that a benefit or not. The explanation of that has come in detail: that they wanted a gradual progression from compromise and his (ﷺ) leniency with them, to what follows it of the suspension of the call.

Ibn Jarir supported this by his saying: "These polytheists wished, O Muhammad, that you would be soft toward them in your religion, by your response to them to inclining toward their gods, so that they would be soft toward you in your worship of your God," as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little﴾ [al-Isra: 74]. End of quote.

What supports what Ibn Jarir said is what has come regarding the occasion of revelation of Surah (al-Kafirun):

(p-254) So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers, ﴾ ﴿I do not worship what you worship, ﴾ ﴿Nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ ... the surah [al-Kafirun: 1-3].

And what is explicit in their intention by compromise, and the motive behind it, and the answer to them, has come clarified in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109], then He said, may He be exalted, explaining the position of the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding this attempt, in His saying: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109].

Allah has brought His command as a judge between him and them. Here it may be said that every compromise in religion with the polytheists falls under this subject.

Then after His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not obey every oft-swearing contemptible one﴾ comes an indication that they are not to be obeyed in their compromise, and that they will expend everything in their power to promote their compromise, even by excessive swearing. And there is a difference between compromise in religion and kindness in worldly matters, or cooperation and exchange of worldly benefits, as we previously mentioned at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 8] and what follows. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾

This is a rhetorical question of denial (istifham inkari), indicating that he did not ask them for any reward for his call to them.

Allah, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for my kinship (al-mawaddah fi al-qurba)﴾ [al-Shura: 23]. Thus the reward that is asked about in this interrogation is the material reward, in wealth and the like.

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) has already dealt, in a thorough discussion at His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you any wealth for it; my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Hud: 29] in Surah Hud, with the question of taking a reward for the call from all the Messengers (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all), and with the question of taking a wage for acts whose origin is a favour from Allah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was suppressing [his grief].﴾

He does not specify here who the companion of the fish is, nor his call while he was suppressing [his grief], nor the manner that is forbidden to be like his. But He, exalted is He, has specified the companion of the fish in (al-Saffat) in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers. When he fled to the laden ship...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So the fish swallowed him, while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Saffat: 139–142].

As for the call, Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) said: He, exalted is He, has specified it in surah (al-Anbiya') at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger, thinking that We would not decree [anything] against him. Then he called out within the darknesses: "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87–88].

So the companion of the fish is Yunus, his call is the one mentioned in the verse, and the state of his call was while he was suppressing [his grief].

As for the manner that is forbidden to be like it: it is the condition he was in at the time of the call, namely his anger, while he was suppressing [his grief]. This is a clarification of an aspect of the character of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of his adopting of good conduct, in His saying, exalted is He: "So be patient," i.e., over the harm of your people. Perhaps this is among the special features and distinctive guidance of Allah directed to him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not except through Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 126–127] to the end of the verse. Thus He, exalted is He, has clarified a general virtuous character for the Ummah: in good dealing and forgiveness.

Then He specified the Prophet (ﷺ) with His saying: "and be patient," i.e., do not punish by way of retaliation, even with an equal measure, but be patient. And there was from him (ﷺ) the realization of this, in his return from Thaqif when they harmed him, and Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him, and with him the angel of the mountains, who awaits his command, until he said: ("No, O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know... Indeed, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who will believe in Allah.") So he forgave and was patient, and hoped from Allah for the faith of those who would come forth from their loins.

This is the utmost degree of patience and forgiveness, and the greatest degree of noble character.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had he not been overtaken by a favor from his Lord, he would have been cast onto the bare land while he was blameworthy.﴾

He, may He be exalted, has explained that he was not cast onto the bare land in a blameworthy state; rather, Allah caused a tree to grow over him to shade him and cover him, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine.﴾ [al-Saffat: 146]

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

Surah al-Qalam

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had he not been overtaken by a favor from his Lord, he would have been cast onto the bare land﴾, the verse.

The manner of reconciling this with His saying: ﴿So We cast him onto the bare land﴾ [al-Saffat: 145] has already been discussed.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 50:

Allah's saying: ﴿Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.﴾

[p. 256] He (may He be exalted) explained it by His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Saffat: 147–148]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, "Indeed, he is a madman."﴾ ﴿But it is not except a Reminder to the worlds.﴾

In this there is a return of the end of the surah to its beginning. The disbelievers, when they hear the Reminder, fix their eyes upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and accuse him of madness. The refutation of them is that what they heard is not the raving of a madman, but is only a Reminder to the worlds. In this there is also a preference for the view that the intended "blessing of your Lord" at the beginning of the surah (﴿You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman﴾) is none other than what He revealed to him of the Reminder.
